item.title: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries
item.content:encoded:
总结:NVIDIA 扩展覆盖语言、机器人、生物学和量子计算领域的开放模型家族，助力欧洲各行业构建主权AI应用。

NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries

The portfolio includes the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models; new NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new NVIDIA Kumo family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; NVIDIA Cosmos 3.5 world models; NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; NVIDIA BioNeMo for healthcare and scientific discovery; and NVIDIA Ising for quantum computing. 

The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control.

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

 

NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries

NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition, including European partners Black Forest Labs, H-Company and Mistral.

Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. Dassault Systèmes, Domyn, Dream, Palantir’s customers, Salesforce, SAP, Shopify, Synopsys and WPP, as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents.

A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery, AgileRL, AI21, Alice, Applied Compute, Baseten, CoreWeave, Distil Labs, EON, Fastino, Fireworks, Google Cloud, Mercor, Multiverse Computing, Nebius, Handshake AI, Plurai, Prime Intellect, River.AI, Scale AI, Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads.

NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data

NVIDIA Kumo open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation, Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task.

Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes NVIDIA Kumo Structured, with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and NVIDIA Kumo Engine, an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models. 

Cognite, Coinbase, Databricks, DoorDash, Revolut and Tubi are among the first to work with Kumo models to accelerate development. Snowflake customers are already using Kumo models to accelerate AI development in industries including advertising, energy, financial services and retail.

NVIDIA Cosmos Accelerates Robotics Training and Simulation

NVIDIA Cosmos is a family of open world foundation models that helps developers build robots, autonomous vehicles and vision agents that understand and interact with the physical world. 

NVIDIA is introducing new Cosmos post-training and optimization tools to help developers improve world models using less compute, along with simulation checkpoints for evaluating behavior in interactive driving and robotic manipulation scenarios before real-world testing.

NVIDIA is also introducing Cosmos Data Factory — comprising blueprints and core agent skills — to help developers curate, label, generate and evaluate training data for driving scenarios, product defects, image augmentation and event generation. Developers can use complete workflows or individual capabilities with agents coordinating the process. 

Porsche with Voxel51, ANYbotics with Encord, Zalando and CEVA Logistics with Sereact, and Siemens are using Cosmos Data Factory to create high-quality, diverse training datasets and improve model precision.

NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Brings Real-Time Reasoning to Autonomous Vehicles

NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a compact reasoning model that brings real-time scene understanding and motion planning directly into autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge’s Nemotron-based foundation and optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor platform, it helps developers bring advanced driving capabilities into vehicles with lower computing requirements.

NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina Advances Protein Design 

NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina is an open protein design model from NVIDIA and the Baker Lab at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design. 

The model generates protein sequences and 3D structures to help researchers design proteins that bind to difficult targets, assemble into complex structures and bind to small molecules. 

NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina delivers leading performance across more than 10 protein design tasks and generates designs about 13x faster than RFdiffusion3 in a benchmark of 200 amino acid proteins. Researchers can use the model through agents to generate and evaluate candidates against design goals and molecular constraints, then choose which designs to test in the lab. 

NVIDIA Ising Accelerates Quantum Development

The NVIDIA Ising family of open models provides a common, extensible foundation to speed the breakthroughs needed to develop useful quantum supercomputers, from real-time hardware calibration to error correction, across different qubit modalities and tailored to individual hardware needs. 

IQM Quantum Computers is using Ising to calibrate its quantum processors, showcasing how specialized open calibration models outperform large general-purpose models. SEEQC is combining the NVIDIA NVQLink platform and Ising with its unique Digital Link to meet the low-latency requirements needed for real-time quantum error correction.

AWS is making NVIDIA Ising readily available to researchers by integrating the model family into AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS). While decoding is typically performed on classical hardware colocated with the quantum processor due to latency requirements, the AWS PCS integration lets researchers build on Ising prior to deployment.

  • NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever open models are available on Hugging Face, various partner platforms, and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice on build.nvidia.com.
  • NVIDIA Kumo open models are available on Hugging Face and optimized and packaged as an NVIDIA NIM microservice for production inference on build.nvidia.com.
  • NVIDIA Cosmos is now openly available on Hugging Face and GitHub, and through select inference partners.
  • NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge will be available for download on GitHub and Hugging Face later this month.
  • The NVIDIA BioNeMo open model RFD4-Proteina is available on build.nvidia.com and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as on GitHub, Hugging Face and through select inference partners. 
  • NVIDIA Ising is available on GitHub, Hugging Face and build.nvidia.com.

item.title: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote
item.content:encoded:
总结:总结：黄仁勋在GTC柏林发表主题演讲，宣布NVIDIA将与欧洲企业深化AI合作，推动欧洲迈向AI工业革命。

Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events.

Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle.

GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. 

Huang Takes the Stage

Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. 

The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said.

 

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

 

AI is a five-layer cake, Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application. 

“Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid.

“To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.”

 

The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor

Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure. 

“This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.” 

He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings.

Next, Huang announced NVIDIA DSX POD, a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready. 

“This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.”

The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power.

Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem

Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful. 

He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools.

“The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored.

NVIDIA’s answer is the new NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents, a full-stack design built on NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect.


That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said.

Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage

Huang presented NVIDIA’s open models as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs. 

NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI. 

“We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.”

NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.”

“You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.”

NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer

Huang then introduced the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases. 

He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new NVIDIA Kumo models for making predictions from structured data.

“Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said.

NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents

Huang then described NVIDIA CUDA-X as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work. 

NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it. 

Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work.

“CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said. 

Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering

A video showcased NVIDIA Agent Toolkit bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples: 

At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab. 

At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor. 

And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design.

“And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.” 

Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure

Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure. 

He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia after nearly eight years of work.

“Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. It will enhance our spectrum efficiency tremendously.” 

AI Moves Into the Treatment Room

Healthcare and life sciences leaders are building on NVIDIA technologies to advance drug discovery and expand patient care.

For example, NVIDIA and Siemens Healthineers are developing AI-enabled radiation therapy. 

Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves.

Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting.

“The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.” 

The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem

Huang said the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets, with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services. 

Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.

In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles at scale.

Volkswagen’s van, JLR, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz’s next-generation vehicles will be Hyperion-compatible, Huang announced, saying, “Welcome to Hyperion.”

A Reference Humanoid for Robotics Researchers

Huang then announced Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days. 

The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components.
“This is a great starting point,” Huang said. 

It builds on NVIDIA’s open physical AI stack — Isaac Capture for data collection, GR00T models for robot intelligence, Isaac Lab for simulation-based training, Isaac OS for runtime — and NVIDIA’s open physical AI dataset. Partners including Agility Robotics, Figure, KUKA and NEURA Robotics are already building on the same platform.

Personal AI Gets a New Machine

Huang closed by discussing RTX Spark laptops, which launched last week, bringing together RTX graphics and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform in slim, premium Windows PCs for accelerated creation, immersive gaming and powerful local AI. 

He compared its 1 petaflop of performance and 128GB of memory with the DGX-1 he delivered to OpenAI in 2016 — then made the difference in size the punchline:

“In the year 2016, I delivered 1 petaflop and 128GB … to a small company called OpenAI,” Huang said, holding up the compact machine in front of the audience. “This is 1 petaflop and 128GB. The only difference, of course, is that I can hold this like this, and DGX-1 took two people to carry upstairs.”

Huang then showed a video of an agent helping train Hugging Face’s Microduck: it set up a course and simulated the robot in Isaac Sim, sent training jobs to the cloud, then brought the learned policy back to RTX Spark for evaluation before deploying it to the physical robot.

A flock of four Microducks joined Huang onstage, sitting down, standing up and even taking a nap on cue. He explained that they were created on RTX Spark, trained in the cloud and learned their skills in simulation.

“You were created on RTX Spark … [we] trained you in the cloud on a whole bunch of NVIDIA supercomputers, and you learned your skills right here on RTX Spark and the digital twin,” Huang told them.

The Full Lineup

With the Microducks gathered around him, Huang recapped the keynote: Europe is building its AI economy, AI factories are evolving to run agents and physical AI is the next frontier.

“So that’s it,” Huang said. “Everybody can build agents. Every company in Europe will become an AI company … and we’re going to have a thriving AI economy here in Europe.”

To close, Huang had one more surprise: a Eurovision-style musical send-off that turned the keynote’s themes into a comic recap. 

The lyrics raced from OpenShell’s guardrails — “No credentials. Access dismissed” and “Sentry on BlueField never clocks off” — to physical AI, where robot training was likened to “college for robots without student loans.” 

The punchline: “You can’t spell fungible without fun.” A saxophone solo led into a rousing “We are Europa” chorus.

“Let’s work together to build Europe’s AI economy and put AI to work,” Huang said, closing out his talk. “Have a great GTC.”

item.title: Germany Wants to Lead the World in Industrial AI: How NVIDIA Will Help
item.content:encoded:
总结:英伟达与德国政府签署合作意向，将助力德国以工业AI和制造业优势打造世界领先的工业人工智能生态。

In the cavernous hall of Kraftwerk, a former power station in Berlin, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang sat down to discuss Germany’s AI roadmap, and in particular, the industrial applications of AI.

Huang opened by tracing NVIDIA’s longstanding relationship with German industry, beginning with gaming systems, workstations and automotive design in the early 2000s and leading to today’s partnerships in autonomous vehicle development and digital twins for manufacturing.

The conversation focused on how Germany can make the most of the AI revolution by playing to its strengths in manufacturing and automotive — and by encouraging AI adoption across the country’s ecosystem of small and medium-sized companies.

Earlier in the day, as part of the Invest in Germany Summit, Chancellor Merz, the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy and the Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space signed a Joint Declaration of Intent with NVIDIA.

The German federal government’s aim is to merge traditional German engineering and manufacturing expertise with cutting-edge research and AI technology. The declaration sets out an agreement to work on a joint initiative with NVIDIA to advance cutting edge AI models for physical AI.

Formalizing and expanding NVIDIA’s collaboration with Germany’s federal government and its “Industry 4.0 Platform,” which is comprised of representatives from politics, industry, research and trade associations, helps achieve the government’s stated goal to “systematically bring industrial AI into widespread use and to establish a state-of-the-art industrial AI ecosystem in Europe.”

Germany’s Ambition to Integrate AI With Industry

Merz and Huang dug into industrial AI and how NVIDIA can help Germany lead the way. The German Chancellor first laid out his government’s ambition.

“We are fully committed to be one of the most advanced places in the world, not just in the European Union, but in the world to work with AI, to integrate AI into our industry,” Merz said. “I’m really optimistic that we will be one of the leading, if not the leading, country in the world in terms of the spread of AI for all the companies — our manufacturers, machinery, automotive industry and suppliers of the automotive industry. I think this is a great opportunity.”

Merz called out the leaders of the small and medium businesses — the Mittelstand — in the audience. 

“The biggest advantage we have in Germany is our so-called Mittelstand,” Merz said. “Please open your doors for AI to make use of your data. This is a real secret and a real advantage for Germany to make use of all the data which is already available in our companies.”

Huang agreed, and praised Germany’s world-class expertise in manufacturing companies both large and small, as well as its math and science excellence. That national expertise and knowledge is what sets the German economy apart, he said, and AI will only amplify it.

“That knowledge belongs to you,” Huang said. “It cannot be replaced. AI can only augment your capability, it will not replace your capability. Take advantage of the technology. It’s a new instrument.”

Germany’s expertise with physical technologies is a differentiator, Huang and Merz agreed, and a powerful accelerator for the German economy when AI is included.

“If we are successful in bringing these two aspects and parts of the business of the future together,” Merz said. “I’m really very optimistic that Germany can be one of the most successful economies in the world.”

Huang described AI’s impact across virtually every industry as a new industrial revolution. 

“This industrial revolution is so mighty, so powerful,” Huang said. “In the Chancellor’s words, you are re-engineering Germany. This is your chance to do it well.”

Merz envisioned a regular reunion with Huang to assess the progress Germany is making with AI.

“I would like to see him regularly, let’s say at least once a year, and discuss the progress we made,” Merz said, “And see a guy sitting in my office being extremely happy about Germany as a place to invest.” 

NVIDIA’s Investments in Germany

Huang also announced new investments in four German startups, part of a nearly $10 billion commitment by NVIDIA to support companies, universities, research institutions and more across Europe. 

NVIDIA has been investing across Germany’s startup ecosystem, supporting leading technology companies including n8n, Neura Robotics and Black Forest Labs. 

 Today, Huang announced new planned investments in Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace. 

Agile Robots, a Munich-based robotics company, builds AI-powered robots, from robotic arms to its Agile ONE humanoid, for manufacturing, logistics and healthcare.

Avelios Medical, a Munich-based healthcare technology startup, develops an AI-native hospital information system that serves as the core system of record for clinical and administrative workflows, integrating AI directly into hospital operations to free up doctors and nurses to deliver better patient care.

Mirelo, a German startup, develops AI models that generate sound effects, speech and music for video, helping creators and production teams produce high-quality audio that perfectly matches their visuals on screen.

Reflex Aerospace, a Berlin-based space scaleup, designs and builds high-performance satellites ready for launch in about 12 months instead of years. 

Siemens and NVIDIA Advance Autonomous Manufacturing; Record-Breaking Quantum Simulation

Earlier in the day, Siemens announced it’s partnering with NVIDIA to advance AI-driven, autonomous factories. Siemens showcased new AI solutions at its Erlangen factory, advancing its role as a global blueprint for autonomous manufacturing. Fully virtual production ramp-up reduces engineering effort by up to 85%, while agent-based production planning enables more adaptive manufacturing and cost savings of up to 20%.

NVIDIA researchers used JUPITER, Europe’s largest supercomputer at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, to run a record-breaking simulation of a fault-tolerant quantum computer. The 104-qubit simulation is the largest and most detailed of its kind to date.

总结:NVIDIA携手欧洲广播联盟及Adobe等合作伙伴，推动智能体在媒体领域的安全与主权化应用。

At a creative industry event that took place today in Berlin — hosted in collaboration with Adobe, Bertelsmann, NVIDIA and UFA — the latest advancements in intelligent media were on display.

Key to the news: the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) is collaborating with NVIDIA to expand its sovereign framework with cloud, open models and integration partners, while Adobe Frame.io is accelerating video agent search capabilities with NVIDIA GPUs, helping German TV and film producer UFA find the right moments faster.

Read more about both announcements below.

Sovereign Clouds and Open Models Built for European Broadcasters

The EBU and NVIDIA are expanding the sovereign standards they introduced last year for European public service media. The initiative now brings in sovereign cloud providers, open model developers and systems integrators to define how broadcasters can deploy agents while keeping control of their data, infrastructure, models and security.
 

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

 

The EBU is the world’s leading alliance of public service media, with over 115 member organizations in more than 55 countries reaching over 1 billion people. As agents move into newsrooms, production and audience services, those broadcasters need a foundation that protects editorial independence, data sovereignty and national resilience.

The expanded initiative is turning those principles into deployable services. It’ll define requirements and reference architectures for where workloads run, how data is governed, which models power services and how systems stay secure throughout their lifecycle.

“These standards give EBU members a shared foundation to strengthen resilience, retain control and deliver accountable advanced services that sustain audience trust,” said Antonio Arcidiacono, chief technology and innovation officer at the EBU.

Cloud providers will map the standards to sovereign deployment options: 

  • Microsoft will bring expertise from Microsoft Sovereign Cloud, including Azure Local and Foundry Local, so broadcasters can process sensitive editorial material locally and keep critical services running when external connectivity is down.
  • Nebius offers a platform for broadcasters to train, fine-tune and run their own models on European infrastructure.

Open models give broadcasters the visibility to inspect, evaluate and adapt AI for local languages, archives and editorial policies. NVIDIA Nemotron open models provide a foundation broadcasters can customize for domain-specific applications and public-service requirements.

“Sovereign cloud infrastructure and open models can help Europe’s public service media innovate while protecting data, editorial independence and cultural diversity,” said Delphine Ernotte, CEO of France Télévisions and president of the EBU.

Media-specific consulting and systems integration provided from Qvest and other system integrators to ensure that reference architectures are practical, interoperable and deployable in real world broadcast environments. 

Adobe Frame.io Speeds Video Search With NVIDIA Accelerated Computing

Also at the event, Adobe is highlighting its latest enhancements that help creatives search through video data faster.

Adobe is using NVIDIA accelerated computing to help creative teams find and work with video content faster. Its GPU-accelerated search pipeline uses NVIDIA NVDEC for video decoding, TensorRT for optimized AI inference and the CUDA platform for preprocessing and embedding generation. 

Adobe is also advancing GPU-accelerated media ingest using NVIDIA NVENC and NVDEC to accelerate video encoding and decoding, helping production teams process growing media libraries more efficiently.  

The results: about 5x faster embedding generation, up to 4x higher throughput and up to 5x lower latency for search processing. A new two-frame-per-second proxy, about 80% smaller than the 360p version it replaces, cuts storage and transfer while keeping the visual detail search needs.

That speed matters for UFA, one of Germany’s leading film and TV producers. It delivers more than 3,500 hours of programming a year, including the daily drama “Gute Zeiten, schlechte Zeiten.” When editors build a recap or flashback, they may need a specific reaction or unresolved exchange from as far back as 15 years — something file names and folders can’t surface.

Frame.io semantic search finds moments inside videos by concept, action or setting, and hybrid search adds notes, transcripts and approval status. An editor can search for “a character looking concerned,” narrow by character name and filter to approved footage, then move straight into review.

The work is part of a broader Adobe and NVIDIA collaboration that also spans Adobe Substance 3D, Firefly Foundry and 3D digital twin workflows for enterprises.

item.title: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models
item.content:encoded:
总结:英伟达推出高效的新模型 Super VL 和 Bolt，扩展 Nemotron 系列，覆盖从数据中心到桌面的智能体部署。

NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents.

Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents.

Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23.

The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. 

Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. 

Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. 

Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. 

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size

Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition, delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count.

As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. 

Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build.

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Agentic Intelligence at the Edge

Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications.

Relative to other models with a similar memory footprint, it provides a good balance of intelligence and speed: smart enough to get most jobs done, yet much faster than the smartest models.

 

With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench, and the #2 open model for BrowseComp.

Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. 

Adoption of Custom Super Intelligence

Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments. 

Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications.

Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream, sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions.

Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include: 

  • Atlassian, for tasks like agentic search across apps such as Jira and Confluence.
  • CrowdStrike, which is customizing the model for agentic blue teaming in enterprise security.
  • Dassault Systèmes, powering engineering design and simulation. 
  • Perplexity, for search and agentic tasks in Perplexity Search and Computer.
  • Salesforce, which is customizing Nemotron to power AI agents that digitize and automate complex government workflows in secure customer environments through Missionforce Operations.
  • Synopsys software for semiconductor design verification interoperates with the model.

What Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Actually Sees

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents. 

It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision. 

Open for Maximum Control, Security, and Privacy

Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes.

Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions.

In insurance, for example, a customized agent can scan claims for fraud markers on repeat. In financial services, an agent can review credit scores and flag activity against an organization’s own lending criteria. The model stays on premises. The data stays private.

Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments.

NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use, finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym.

NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements.

And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM.

Runs on DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX 

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on DGX Spark, DGX Station,  RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments.

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth, and vLLM. Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs, DGX Spark, DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations.

item.title: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute
item.content:encoded:
总结:NVIDIA 通过开放学习资源、合作与计算能力，为欧洲科学界拓展先进技术的获取途径。

Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation. 

But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both. 

At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community. 

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements


NVIDIA is joining the campaign, providing:

  • Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms
  • Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources
  • Skills, training and technical support
  • Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent
  • Support for startups and ecosystem development

“Europe’s ambition in AI in science can only become reality if we bring together the strengths of our research community, industry and other partners,” Ekaterina Zaharieva, European Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation. “Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers access to the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.”

Open Models

NVIDIA’s pledge begins with open source technology. 

NVIDIA has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open source software projects spanning large language models, healthcare, robotics, climate science, physical AI, autonomous vehicles and scientific research. The models and datasets are available on Hugging Face and GitHub.

Building on this open ecosystem, researchers can build agentic reasoning capabilities with NVIDIA Nemotron — a family of architectures, open weights, open source models, training data and recipes — and scientific software including NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo libraries, NVIDIA Earth-2 models and NVIDIA ALCHEMI NIM microservices to accelerate research across biology, chemistry, molecular design, weather and climate, energy, engineering, physics and material sciences. 

Skills and Training 

Building advanced intelligence capability across Europe requires knowledge that travels as freely as compute. 

The NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute has launched a new open source courseware hub with hands-on course materials covering accelerated computing and deep learning — freely downloadable and openly licensed, with no enrollment, fees or deadline. 

Modular by design, the courses can be adapted for university curricula, supercomputing center bootcamps or developer community events, and serve as a direct bridge to NVIDIA’s broader training and certification programs.

Access to Compute

NVIDIA is collaborating with cloud infrastructure partners and European national AI factories — including in France, Spain and Sweden — to open new routes for startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to access sovereign European compute and services. 

The NVIDIA Inception program for startups provides access to compute resources and technical support, lowering the barrier to entry for startups seeking high-performance infrastructure and technological education. 

AI2F in France is the first AI factory to have collaborated with the Inception program for four months, demonstrating strong results.

The BSC AI Factory ran a pilot initiative and is now rolling out its first full accelerator program, with growing interest from other European national AI factories in replicating the model in 2027. Beyond startup support, this program is designed to contribute to a broader strategic objective: building self-sustaining AI ventures in Spain and Europe.

Sweden AI Factory, one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and SMEs enterprises across sectors including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming. 

Finally, EuroHPC supercomputing centers such as CINECA and JSC provide academia and startups with free access to NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and services for open research. NVIDIA complements this access with office hours, bootcamps and hackathons that help researchers fine-tune models on their own datasets.

As an example, NVIDIA is co-organizing an European AI hackathon this month alongside Austrian Scientific Computing, the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart and The Cyprus Institute, for Pharos-CY.

AI Infrastructure Expansion

To top it all off, NVIDIA is powering Europe’s most ambitious expansion of AI infrastructure to date, with 35 supercomputers currently in development across the continent — the largest single-year buildout of supercomputing capacity Europe has ever seen.

Together, these systems will equip over 3 million researchers with next-generation infrastructure, accelerating discovery across domains from climate science and drug development to materials research and beyond.

Explore NVIDIA technologies for science and open source courseware, and find hands-on training through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute.

item.title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing
item.content:encoded:
总结:北欧国家在先进计算技术方面取得突破，将如何释放其潜力？

The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent.

Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems.

The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application.

Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub

The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry.  

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

 

The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Hyperstack, Nscale, Verda and Volta. 

In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment.

Nordic-Built Intelligence

Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure.

Spotify, which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query.

ABB Robotics developed RobotStudio HyperReality using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%.

Finnish telecom company Elisa is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses. 

Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA

Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models.

Stilta is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives Stilta the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold.

ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron, built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish.

Agaton, a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions.

Klang, a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source NVIDIA NeMo framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face.

Embedl, founded in Gothenburg and a member of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity.

Sweden AI Factory — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming.

Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors

In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories.

Autonomous freight company Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on NVIDIA Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using the NVIDIA Halos safety system and NVIDIA Cosmos open world models.

Meanwhile, Toyota Material Handling Europe — the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and SoftServe, Toyota Material Handling Europe is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams.

Norrsken Foundation and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027. 

Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing

Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform.

Stockholm-based FirstQFM used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a QuantWare quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated.

item.title: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem
item.content:encoded:
总结:英伟达宣布对英国初创企业生态系统进行新投资，支持多个AI和量子计算领域的创新公司。

Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work.

The scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems.

NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. 

NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK

NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research, Ineffable Intelligence, Synthesia, Wayve and many more. 

Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz, Foresight, Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane.

Boltz, a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines.

Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue.

Hiverge, a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning.

Prima Mente, a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS.

Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use.

In addition, NVIDIA is partnering with the Earthshot Prize, joining as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to bring compute and technical expertise to innovators working on solutions for the world’s greatest climate and sustainability challenges.

 

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

 

Technology Leaders Pioneer Intelligent Solutions Across the UK

In energy, Fuse Energy is moving its customer AI onto its own in-house infrastructure, built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra, delivering faster, more responsive support to over 450,000 U.K. households. 

Meanwhile, sovereign AI company Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK — an open source dataset of one million synthetic personas representing the UK’s demographic, regional and cultural diversity — helping developers build fairer, more representative AI systems.

Healthcare 

In healthcare, OneAdvanced is deploying what it calls the U.K.’s first and most advanced fine-tuned LLM for Primary Care AI-triage — built with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software and open models — supporting millions of National Health Service patients.

Heidi has now integrated NVIDIA Nemotron open models to give clinicians faster access to trusted medical evidence. 

Speechmatics is deploying Oak, a multilingual medical speech recognition model, using NVIDIA Triton Inference — giving healthcare organizations control over where sensitive patient audio is processed. 

Apian, Synnovis and NVIDIA are teaming up to use advanced computing and digital simulations using NVIDIA Cosmos to help hospital robots handle the heavy lifting of moving lab samples, freeing up medical staff to focus on patient care.  

Danaher and NVIDIA are collaborating to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of discovery by bringing accelerated computing, scientific and physical AI into laboratory workflows and instruments. Danaher’s recently announced AI-powered autonomous lab — designed to deliver up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents — is using NVIDIA BioNeMo open models within its AI-driven protein design workflows, data and automation technologies that connect design with experimental feedback. 

Smart Cities

On the civic side, Liverpool City Region is building an NVIDIA-powered “City Brain” — a sovereign AI strategy designed as a blueprint for dozens of Unitary Authorities across the U.K. 

Digital Jersey, Innovation City Belfast and Tees Valley Combined Authority are each exploring how trusted AI compute can serve communities and public services.

Financial Services

In financial services, LSEG and NVIDIA are bringing GPU-accelerated market analytics to global institutions. 

Revolut introduced PRAGMA earlier in the year — a foundation model for banking event sequences, pre-trained on 26 million anonymised user histories. PRAGMA has moved from research to real-time scaling.

Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM, a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable AI. And Starling is developing a banking foundation model trained on Civo’s U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure. 

NatWest is collaborating with NVIDIA on Nemotron Voice to better understand how banking customers across the U.K. speak, while Modulr is deploying a network of agents using Nemotron for distinct parts of payment operations. 

Quantum

Quantum is moving from research to systems deployable alongside classical AI, and the U.K. is at the heart of this shift. 

Riverlane has shown how GPUs can accelerate decoder recalibration workflows used in quantum error correction, helping decoder performance keep pace with real-time changes in quantum hardware behaviour. The work forms part of a broader collaboration exploring how AI, accelerated computing and quantum error-correction technologies can work together to support future quantum systems.

Together, these announcements showcase how enterprises, organizations and startups in the U.K. are fostering innovation across the nation. This includes more than 3,100 U.K. companies that are a part of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups.

item.title: All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark
item.content:encoded:
总结:NVIDIA推出RTX Spark，整合游戏PC、创意工作室和个人AI超级计算机功能，支持本地与云端AI混合路由。

NVIDIA RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — a reinvention combining the capabilities of a gaming PC, a creative studio and a personal AI supercomputer into a single superchip. With up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute, RTX Spark delivers the full stack of NVIDIA RTX and CUDA technologies for creators, developers and gamers, while unlocking a new paradigm in personal computing via powerful local AI agents.

Last week, NVIDIA and Microsoft announced that RTX Spark laptops will be available on Friday, Oct. 16. Ahead of the launch, NVIDIA and its ecosystem partners are rolling out new software features and performance optimizations to expand what’s possible with local AI on RTX Spark. 

New and upcoming RTX Spark updates — among the thousands of apps, games and models available at launch — include: 

  • New agent features, models and tools that enhance local agents on RTX Spark: 
    • Updates to top agent apps including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy streamline setup on RTX Spark, improve security with OpenShell and Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), and enable hybrid local and cloud AI routing.
    • The NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B model, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark, releases on Thursday, Oct. 15. 
    • NVIDIA PAIR moves out of beta and adds llama.cpp support.
  • Top creative apps optimized for RTX Spark:
    • Up to 2x performance is coming soon to Adobe’s top apps. NVIDIA and Adobe have collaborated to rearchitect Photoshop for GPU-accelerated compositing and Premiere for playback, rendering, effects and more.
    • The NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 release brings new Video Super Resolution, Video Frame Generation, offline file processing and agent Model Context Protocol (MCP) controls to the app.
    • NVIDIA RTX Video Frame Generation and high dynamic range (HDR) capabilities are available now in ComfyUI to accelerate AI generative video workflows.
    • NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction will be available in Blender 5.3 in November to improve interactivity in the viewport.
  • Developer tools are now ready for RTX Spark:
    • Top developer frameworks are now available for RTX Spark, including PyTorch, Python and CUDA, as well as all CUDA libraries. 
    • GitHub Copilot, Pi and other coding agents are now optimized for RTX Spark.
    • Llama.cpp adds support for decision models, and releases a Windows app.
  • Hundreds of top games and anti-cheat are supported on RTX Spark, plus:
    • A 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model arrives Friday, Oct. 16, and a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation is available today via the NVIDIA App beta.
    • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, the third-generation small language model (SLM) for NVIDIA ACE AI game characters, releases Friday, Oct. 23.
    • The latest RTX Remix update, including DLSS 5 support, releases on Friday, Oct. 23.

Advancing Local AI Agents With New Apps, Models and Tools

AI is changing the way people interact with PCs. Agent popularity skyrocketed this year, with projects such as OpenClaw and Hermes topping popularity charts on GitHub. Local large language models (LLMs) surpassed the intelligence threshold to power agents, with models like Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next catching up to frontier cloud models released just a few months ago. As a result, local LLM downloads are already 5x higher than all of last year.

From models to agent harnesses to security to tools, NVIDIA is partnering closely with the local AI ecosystem to make RTX Spark the ideal hardware to run local agents. 

Local AI Agents Made Easy On RTX Spark

From the first boot of RTX Spark, users will be greeted with a “Getting Started” screen to choose and install their agent app.

These agents will come with new, secure sandboxing technology thanks to NVIDIA OpenShell and MXC. MXC delivers operating system-level security, while OpenShell makes it simpler for agents to adopt MXC and adds advanced capabilities such as credential protection and security monitoring. Hermes Agent will integrate granular OpenShell controls and MXC by the end of the month. OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot now support MXC.

After installing an agent, setting up local AI is also now seamless in GitHub Copilot, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy. The apps will recommend an optimized local model and settings configuration for RTX Spark, and set it all up for users in a few clicks.

Many users want the best of both worlds — local models for free iteration, and cloud models for frontier intelligence. NVIDIA Switchyard, an open source model router library, enables agents to intelligently route queries between local and cloud LLMs, allowing the user to minimize cloud usage but still obtain similar results to just running on cloud. Hermes will be adding Switchyard later in October, and other agents like Perplexity Computer and GitHub Copilot have integrated their own routing solutions.

Software providers have made it simple for agents to connect to top Windows apps, with easy-to-use MCP libraries and command line interfaces (CLIs). NVIDIA has also now made available MCPs for its applications, including NVIDIA App, Broadcast, PAIR, Omniverse, RTX Remix and a large library of CUDA-X Skills. 

NVIDIA is also releasing AI playbooks for RTX Spark, available on Friday, Oct 16. Users can set up their first agent, build an AI chief of staff, configure their system for development or design a creative assistant.

Meet Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B: Built for Local Agents on RTX Spark

NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, available Thursday, Oct. 15, is a new LLM purpose-built for running local agents on RTX Spark. 

This model is a 74B parameter, 9B-active-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, packed into 24GB using 2-bit quantization with advanced quantization-aware training techniques to retain quality. It aims to achieve the optimal balance between speed and intelligence, being faster than most popular dense models while smarter than most popular MoE models with a similar memory footprint.

Users will be able to run Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B at launch through llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio. It will also be directly accessible via agents such as Hermes and OpenClaw.  

Like other Nemotron models, Bolt 74B is fully open source — including training data, weights and recipes — so developers can fine-tune and customize their own agents.

The Perfect PAIR

Local AI doesn’t have to run on just one PC. NVIDIA PAIR, a personal AI router, is officially moving out of beta today, making it easier to tap into the total AI compute of compatible PCs on a local network. The free, open source software tool automatically discovers and connects devices, installs AI models and inference engines, and distributes AI workloads across available systems.

The official release adds llama.cpp support, direct model downloads from Hugging Face, customizable inference engine settings and RTX Spark support, along with a variety of inference and user experience improvements. 

PAIR works on Windows, Linux and macOS. Developers can contribute to the open source project via Github — just one month after the initial PAIR release, the community has already contributed over 10 features and fixes to the release. 

Sparking Creativity

RTX Spark brings over 130 accelerated apps, CUDA for fast video and image generation, and RTX technologies such as DLSS, NVENC and OptiX to advanced content creation workflows — all in a thin and light laptop with on-the-go performance.

Adobe Accelerates Creative Applications for RTX Spark

Adobe is optimizing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, for RTX Spark, delivering up to 2x faster AI, editing, color and effects across creative workflows. 

In Photoshop, GPU-accelerated compositing makes complex image editing faster and more responsive, with improvements to the Remove Tool and effects such as Light Leaks. Premiere accelerates demanding video editing tasks, including playback, rendering, color grading and AI-powered features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask. Meanwhile, Substance 3D Painter speeds up texture creation workflows, from baking high-resolution mesh maps to opening, saving and exporting large projects.

The updates will be rolling out in phases, with AI feature optimizations in Photoshop and Premiere now ready in beta, and with Adobe Substance 3D updates coming soon. Opt in to the beta to get access to the RTX Spark-optimized builds. 

Latest NVIDIA Broadcast Brings New AI Effects to Live and Recorded Content

Available for download now, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 runs natively on RTX Spark, and adds new RTX Video Super Resolution and Frame Generation AI effects and Studio Voice profiles.

A new Offline File Processor lets creators apply Broadcast effects to prerecorded content, with many effects running at higher quality since there isn’t a need to maintain real-time performance. The update also introduces a new MCP server and skill that lets local AI agents adjust effects, change settings and process files directly through the Broadcast app.

RTX Video Brings Frame Generation and HDR to ComfyUI

ComfyUI is expanding its RTX Video tools with two new nodes: RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR. It’s also providing the ability to export EXR files, giving creators more ways to enhance AI-generated video.

 

RTX Video Frame Generation increases video frame rates for smoother motion for GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and newer, while RTX Video HDR converts standard dynamic range (SDR) footage to HDR for greater flexibility in color grading. Combined with RTX Video Super Resolution, these tools enable creators to upscale, enhance and refine video within a single ComfyUI workflow.

For example, creators can combine LTX 2.5 with RTX Video Frame Generation and HDR to transform a 1080p, 30 frames-per-second (fps) SDR clip into a smoother 60 fps HDR video exported as EXR files ready for color grading. 

Blender Adds DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction

Blender has released a beta version of its popular 3D editor, adding compatibility for RTX Spark. Download Blender version 5.3 to get access.

Coming next month, Blender will also be adding support for DLSS Ray Reconstruction, allowing for real-time updates in the viewport so artists can navigate a scene while previewing it in real time. 

Code, Text and Deploy From RTX Spark

Developers are moving from writing code to directing AI agents. This new development paradigm is requiring many to spread their work across their laptop, a cloud LLM and a cloud virtual machine, where they test and prototype. 

RTX Spark enables developers to work on one machine, running all their workloads and libraries, testing and prototyping, and deploying. They can now do so directly in Windows with the new Windows Developer Config, which enhances the user experience for devs and installs all the top developer tools — or via Windows Subsystem for Linux, where they can get access to the same packages they’ll use to publish to the cloud.

Developer Tools Are RTX-Spark Ready

NVIDIA has partnered with Microsoft to ensure that developer tools are ready for RTX Spark. Alongside RTX Spark, the community is releasing:

  • The first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm.
  • The first Python build that is native by default on Windows on Arm, with Python 3.15.
  • The first native Conda installer for Windows on Arm, with over 2,000 Conda packages.
  • 97% of the top 15,000 Python wheels are ready, thanks to work with the ecosystem. NVIDIA will be working closely with the community to ready the remaining wheels.

Development is now mostly done by agents. NVIDIA Skills — an open source GitHub repository that teaches agents how to use NVIDIA CUDA-X tools and libraries — lets users develop apps that are accelerated on NVIDIA technologies, even without knowing anything about CUDA.

Coding Agents Are Ready for Local AI

In addition to GitHub Copilot — one of the most popular coding agents, used by millions worldwide — adding support for MXC, it’s updating its model router HydraFusion with support for local models. This enables developers to use their local hardware to reduce token consumption while tapping into frontier intelligence.

Microsoft is making coding models, such as MAI 1.1 Coding Flash, available locally, and adding llama.cpp as a backend to Windows ML — extending the supported models and enabling the latest NVIDIA performance optimizations.

Get started with GitHub Copilot running locally when RTX Spark launches.

Llama.cpp Adds Support for Decision Models, Releases a Windows App

Decision models are the latest breakthrough in AI development. They give AI agents a near-instant way to make decisions, without lengthy reasoning loops. They can choose what to do next, from classifying requests to selecting the next action, up to 200x faster than traditional agents. Decision models are now supported in llama.cpp and Unsloth on RTX Spark and GeForce RTX GPUs.

Llama.cpp is also releasing today Llama Windows, a Windows-native companion app for llama.cpp, enabling an easy-to-use user interface to download and run models locally, without having to go into the command line. This app, like llama.cpp, is optimized for RTX Spark. Learn more on the Hugging Face blog.

Game On: RTX Spark Launches With Hundreds of Top Games and DLSS 5

RTX Spark is ready for gaming, with hundreds of top titles available when laptops launch on Friday, Oct. 16, including CONTROL Resonant, Cyberpunk 2077, Fortnite, Gears of War: E-Day, Genshin Impact, Hogwarts Legacy, Honkai: Star Rail, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, NBA 2K27, World of Warcraft and many more.

NVIDIA has worked to bring the full stack of RTX technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, Remix, G-SYNC and ray tracing, to the new platform, along with collaborating with game developers to enable anti-cheat support for popular multiplayer games. Learn more about gaming on RTX Spark. 

DLSS 5 Brings Neural Rendering to RTX Spark

NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is also coming to RTX Spark on launch day. The technology uses AI to enhance lighting and materials with lifelike detail, making game worlds and characters more realistic while preserving developers’ artistic vision. A new, 2x faster DLSS 5 AI model debuts in NBA 2K27 on Friday, Oct. 16, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x. The faster model will also power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy starting Thursday, Nov. 5, and Where Winds Meet in late November.

DLSS 5 is also coming to NVIDIA RTX Remix on Friday, Oct. 23, so modders can add better materials, lighting and shadows to classic characters and environments, as shown from modder Sparkles/Kim2091 in her in-development project, Fallout 4 RTX.

Read more about DLSS 5 on RTX Spark on GeForce.com.

Game Agents Running Locally on RTX Spark

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is the third-generation SLM for NVIDIA ACE, the suite of technologies for building in-game AI agents that deliver next-generation gaming experiences. The first-generation model was in a public beta earlier this year for PUBG, allowing players to team up with AI teammates, while the more efficient second-generation model previewed in Aniimo at Gamescom, turning standard creatures into voice-responsive companions.

Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B combines natural conversation with multi-turn tool use, instruction following and grounding in application state to power fast local voice and device assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces.

Designed for a low memory footprint and fast time to first token, this model enables responsive local experiences while leaving headroom for applications and other AI models. Its new conversational mode helps keep responses concise and speech-ready, and developers can turn reasoning on or off as needed. 

Starting Friday, Oct. 23, test drive the third-generation Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB inside SkyrimNET, an AI nonplayable character (NPC) modding platform by MinLL for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. SkyrimNET transforms every NPC into an unscripted, interactive character equipped with personal memory, voice and autonomy for dynamic conversations and context-aware quests generated on the fly.

Now compatible with RTX Spark, SkyrimNET supports both cloud and local inference across multiple models, with the latest Nemotron models delivering best-in-class performance for efficient and fast in-game interactions. Download the build on GitHub.

Accelerating Modding Workflows in RTX Remix

As AI agents continue to help modders make their favorite classic games compatible with the RTX Remix renderer, NVIDIA is streamlining asset updates with a major overhaul to its AI-powered texture generation workflow. Launching Friday, Oct. 23, as part of Remix 1.6, ComfyUI Version 2 replaces complex REST application programming interface (API) node connections with a dedicated AI tools layout directly in the sidebar.

This update allows modders and artists to generate physically based rendering materials natively inside RTX Remix with zero API setup required. A new batch processing feature makes it easy to scale beyond single-texture experimentation to full modding projects, while an intuitive presets system lets non-technical creators adjust key settings without touching the node graph. 

Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.
